drilling.title: Drilling Data
drilling.intro: The drill holes of the Exploration module.

steps.1: Add Drill Hole opens a spreadsheet-like sheet: type or paste a block from Excel into the empty rows. The latest 50 holes sit above, locked; click the lock to change one in place, then Save them all at once.
steps.2: Search by hole ID or area, and filter by status.
steps.3: Edit opens the same sheet with that hole already unlocked; the bin icon removes a hole for good.
steps.4: Import uploads thousands of drill holes at once from Excel/CSV (previewed first; rows with errors can be downloaded); Export downloads the list on screen in the same format.

drilling.tip: The hole ID must be unique. Every other field may be left empty and completed later.

1.title: You run the Exploration module
1.body: Drilling Data holds every drill hole: add, edit, search and delete.

2.title: Help is always here
2.body: Press ? at the top of any page for the part of the guide about it.

import.title: Import Drilling Data
import.description: Upload an Excel (.xlsx) or CSV file. Rows are matched by hole ID: new hole IDs are added, existing ones can be updated. At most 50,000 rows, 20 MB.
import.columnsHint: The first row holds the column headers: {columns}. Only Hole ID is required; other columns may be left out. Dates: YYYY-MM-DD or DD/MM/YYYY.
import.updateExisting: Update the {count} drill holes that already exist (same hole ID)
import.updateExistingHint: Empty cells in the file do not erase what is already stored.
import.errorsTitle: {count, plural, one {# row has errors and will not be imported} other {# rows have errors and will not be imported}}
import.moreErrors: Showing {shown} of {total} errors. Download the report for the full list.

sheet.title: Add & change drill holes
